h1: Artino Hotel Silom — 5-min walk to BNH Hospital, a quiet boutique in the heart of Silom
intro: In a Silom neighborhood filled with offices and some of Bangkok's top private hospitals, Artino Hotel Silom sits on the short, quiet Soi Phiphat 2, which opens straight onto Convent Road · the fact that draws most guests here is simple: BNH Hospital is about a 5-minute walk away, making it one of the closest places to stay for patients and family members visiting the hospital · it also sits 4 min from BTS Sala Daeng and 5 min from MRT Si Lom, so getting anywhere in the city is straightforward · the hotel has a rooftop saltwater pool, an on-site restaurant, and free parking — all in an 18-room building where the service feels personal · from about THB 1,700/night.

body.html: Who Artino Hotel Silom is for — the short version: this is a small, 18-room 4-star boutique hotel that trades on its location above all else · it sits on Soi Phiphat 2, a quiet lane off Convent Road, and its two clearest selling points are the roughly 5-minute walk to BNH Hospital and the 4-minute walk to BTS Sala Daeng · from real reviews, the two groups that come here most often are families and companions of patients at BNH Hospital — because being able to walk to the hospital in five minutes, without fighting Bangkok traffic, is exactly the thing you need when someone you care about is being treated nearby — and business travelers or tourists who want a central Silom base that's genuinely easy to reach by sky-train · a third group is people who want a quiet, calm hotel room in the middle of a busy district · the hotel has 18 rooms, which means the staff can genuinely pay attention to every guest, and the atmosphere is closer to a small boutique inn than a big city hotel · reviews consistently single out the location, the friendly staff, and clean rooms as the things that matter here · there are also honest things to say about where it falls short, which I'll cover directly below.

Location and getting around — the hotel's address is 1 Soi Phiphat 2, Convent Road, Silom, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500 · to understand how close it is to BNH Hospital: Soi Phiphat 2 opens straight onto Convent Road, and BNH Hospital sits at 9/1 Convent Road on the same street · walk out of the soi, turn left, and in about 5 minutes and roughly 400 metres you reach the BNH Hospital entrance — no major crossings, no need for a taxi or tuk-tuk · for the sky-train and metro: BTS Sala Daeng is about a 4-minute walk (exit the soi onto Silom Road, the station is right there) and MRT Si Lom is about a 5-minute walk along Convent Road toward the junction · from BTS Sala Daeng you can reach Siam, Asok, Chong Nonsi or Sukhumvit directly, and the MRT links to Hua Lamphong, Sam Yan, and the Airport Rail Link at Makkasan · other nearby points: Silom Road and its restaurants are a 2-minute walk, Patpong night market is 10 minutes on foot, Lumpini Park is about 15 minutes walking, and Silom Complex mall is a few minutes away · for airports, Suvarnabhumi (BKK) is 30–45 minutes by road depending on traffic.

"Super well-located, close to everything, and the staff is incredibly kind and attentive · the location was a 2-minute walk from Silom Road and the BTS was a very short walk away, couldn't ask for more for the price."

Room types and what to expect — Artino has 18 rooms across four types: Standard Room, Superior Room, Deluxe Room, and Large Room · all rooms are relatively compact — Standard and Superior rooms are around 21 sqm, Deluxe and Large rooms around 25 sqm — so this is not the place if you need a big living space or a kitchenette · every room has a double or queen bed, satellite TV, mini fridge and bar, kettle, in-room safe, air-conditioning, and a bathroom with a separate toilet and shower · the Large Room has the added benefit of direct access to the rooftop pool · the decor is modern boutique in style, clean lines, relatively fresh-looking · real reviews are consistent on the positives: clean rooms, comfortable beds, and the quietness of the soi even though you're right in central Silom · the honest negatives come up repeatedly too: the bathrooms are quite small and some guests find the design cramped, with doors that bang noisily in a few rooms; the walls are thin enough to hear the neighboring room; and a handful of reviews mention dampness or a musty smell in certain rooms · if you're sensitive to bathroom size or thin walls, it's worth knowing before you book.

Facilities, rooftop pool, and restaurant — the facility that sets Artino apart from comparable-priced boutique hotels in the area is its rooftop saltwater swimming pool · reviews consistently call it one of the best parts of the hotel — the pool faces directly toward MahaNakhon Tower (the pixelated skyscraper that's become a Bangkok landmark), making for a striking view from the water · the rooftop is good for a morning swim or an evening wind-down, and because the hotel is small the pool is rarely crowded · the on-site restaurant serves breakfast and lunch, and the breakfast format here is worth noting: several reviews praise it as cook-to-order rather than a fixed buffet, with fresh, well-made dishes — a step above what many hotels in this price bracket offer · beyond the pool and restaurant, the hotel has a meeting room that seats 30 guests with a projector, 24-hour front desk, room service, luggage storage, taxi booking, free Wi-Fi throughout the building, and free private parking (limited spaces, must be reserved in advance) · the parking point is significant — free parking in the Silom area is genuinely hard to find.

Service — the consistent standout — across every review platform, the single thing guests mention most often and most warmly is the staff · words like "incredibly kind," "attentive," "helpful with everything" appear again and again · with only 18 rooms the team can learn guests' names, notice when something isn't right, and respond quickly — a real difference from staying in a large hotel where you're one of hundreds · for guests staying because a family member is being treated at BNH Hospital, several reviews specifically mention that staff were understanding, flexible with check-in and check-out timing when hospital appointments ran long, and went out of their way to assist · the other thing guests note about the experience here is the quiet of Soi Phiphat 2 — despite being less than 500 metres from busy Silom Road, the soi itself is calm at night, and several reviews mention sleeping well without street noise.

What real reviews say — the good and the honest — pulling from Booking.com, Trip.com, and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly clear and consistent · on the positive side: excellent location for BNH Hospital, BTS Sala Daeng, and MRT Si Lom; staff who are friendly, kind, and quick; clean rooms and comfortable beds; a genuinely attractive rooftop pool with a MahaNakhon Tower view; good cook-to-order breakfast; free parking that's rare in this area; and a quiet soi in the middle of the city · on the watch-out side: the most-mentioned complaint is the small, awkwardly designed bathroom — several guests say the layout makes it feel cramped, and in some rooms the door swings with a bang; thin walls that carry sound from neighboring rooms; some reports of dampness or smell in certain rooms; and a small number of international reviews describe unexpected or disputed linen-damage charges, which is worth knowing about — take a photo of the room at check-in and verify the bill carefully at check-out · the overall scores sit at 8.3 on Booking.com (Location 9.0 · Staff 9.1 · Comfort 8.7 · Cleanliness 8.5 · Value 8.4), 8.4 on Trip.com from 30 reviews, and 8.2 from 867 reviews on HotelsCombined.

"Location was excellent, very close to BNH Hospital and the BTS — that was the main reason we chose it for our family member's treatment · staff were kind and understanding, the room was clean and quiet, and the rooftop pool was a nice way to relax in the evening after a long day at the hospital."

Pricing and value — Standard Rooms start at around THB 1,700–1,900/night at normal rates (roughly $38–$49 across booking platforms), climbing higher in high season, peak holidays, and when demand from the nearby hospital is strong · Deluxe Rooms run from around THB 2,100 and Large Rooms from around THB 2,400 · measured against other 4-star hotels in the Silom area, Artino's pricing is reasonable for the location and the personal service, particularly given the rooftop pool, free parking, and the unbeatable 5-minute walk to BNH · the trade-off is room size: at 21–25 sqm these are not large rooms, and the bathrooms are clearly on the small side · if you need more space or a kitchen, you'll want to look at serviced apartment hotels in the Silom-Sathorn corridor instead · but if your priority is being close to BNH, easy BTS/MRT access, and a hotel that feels looked-after, the value proposition is strong.

Good to know before you book — a few things make the difference · one: parking — there are free spaces but not many; mention it when you book and confirm by phone before you arrive · two: if you're staying while a family member is at BNH, tell the hotel at the time of booking — staff are familiar with medical-stay guests and can help with flexible check-in/check-out, food requests, and other practical things · three: check the room on arrival, especially for damp and smell, and report anything you're not happy with right away so the team can address it · four: a small number of reviews raise concerns about unexpected damage charges at check-out — photograph the room when you arrive and check your bill carefully before you leave · five: because there are only 18 rooms, this hotel fills quickly around BNH Hospital's busier appointment periods and during Bangkok high season — book ahead with free cancellation if your dates are flexible.

Verdict — Artino Hotel Silom is the right choice for two clear groups of travelers: those who need to be close to BNH Hospital, and those who want a quiet, well-served Silom base that's genuinely a short walk from both the BTS and MRT · the rooftop saltwater pool, the cook-to-order breakfast, the genuinely kind staff, the free parking, and the calm soi are real differentiators at this price in this neighborhood · if you need a large room or a full bathroom, you'll need to look elsewhere · but if BNH proximity and honest, personal service matter to you — and you're happy with a compact but well-run room — Artino earns its place on the shortlist, and the 5-minute walk to the hospital is exactly what it promises.

honestSummary: Artino Hotel Silom is a compact 18-room boutique that earns its place because of location — a 5-minute walk to BNH Hospital, 4 minutes to BTS Sala Daeng, and 5 minutes to MRT Si Lom — combined with staff that guests genuinely like and a rooftop saltwater pool that punches above the hotel's price class · the honest trade-offs are small bathrooms, thin walls, some dampness reports, and a small number of reviews raising concerns about check-out charges · book ahead, check the room on arrival, and photograph it — with those steps taken, most guests leave very satisfied.
honestChecks: If you're staying because of a BNH Hospital visit — the 5-minute walk on Convent Road is exactly what it sounds like: easy and flat · tell the hotel at booking about your schedule, because staff understand medical-stay guests and can flex check-in/check-out timing when hospital appointments run over

If you need a spacious room or a full-size bathroom — rooms are 21–25 sqm and bathrooms are genuinely small; some guests find them cramped · if space matters to you, look at serviced apartment hotels in Silom-Sathorn where you'll get more sqm, a kitchenette, and a bigger bathroom

If you're driving to the hotel — free parking exists but spaces are limited · always mention parking when you reserve and confirm by phone before you leave home — without a reserved spot you'll be parking on the street or in a nearby paid lot in an area where street space is scarce

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Artino Hotel Silom

faq.q: How far is Artino Hotel Silom from BNH Hospital?
faq.a: The hotel is at 1 Soi Phiphat 2, Convent Road, which connects directly onto Convent Road — the same street as BNH Hospital at 9/1 Convent Road · walk out of the soi, turn left, and in about 5 minutes and roughly 300–400 metres you reach the BNH Hospital entrance · no major road crossings are needed, and you don't need a taxi or motorbike · it's one of the closest hotels to BNH in the Silom area.

faq.q: How do I get to BTS Sala Daeng and MRT Si Lom from Artino Hotel Silom?
faq.a: BTS Sala Daeng is about a 4-minute walk — walk out of Soi Phiphat 2, turn right onto Silom Road, and the station entrance is right there at the Sala Daeng intersection · MRT Si Lom is about a 5-minute walk in the other direction along Convent Road toward the junction with Silom Road · from Sala Daeng BTS you can reach Siam, Asok, and Chong Nonsi directly; from MRT Si Lom you can reach Hua Lamphong, Sam Yan, and the Airport Rail Link at Makkasan.

faq.q: What are the room prices at Artino Hotel Silom?
faq.a: Standard Rooms start at around THB 1,700–1,900/night at regular rates · Deluxe Rooms are around THB 2,100 and the Large Room (with direct pool access) is around THB 2,400 · prices rise in high season and on public holidays · because the hotel has only 18 rooms it fills quickly, so book in advance and choose free cancellation if your dates might change.

faq.q: Does Artino Hotel Silom have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — the hotel has a saltwater rooftop pool, which is one of its most praised features · the pool faces toward MahaNakhon Tower, making for a striking backdrop · because the hotel is small the pool is rarely crowded · the Large Room type includes direct access to the rooftop pool.

faq.q: Is there free parking at Artino Hotel Silom?
faq.a: Yes, there is free private parking, but spaces are limited · you must request parking at the time of booking and confirm by phone before you arrive · free parking in the Silom area is unusual — most nearby hotels either charge for it or don't have it at all.

faq.q: Is Artino Hotel Silom a good choice when visiting BNH Hospital?
faq.a: It's one of the best-placed options in the area for exactly this reason · the 5-minute walking route from Soi Phiphat 2 onto Convent Road directly to BNH means no taxi stress, no Bangkok traffic on early-morning appointment days · the hotel is small (18 rooms), staff are consistently praised for being kind and understanding of medical-stay guests, and the soi is quiet for sleeping · tell the hotel at booking that you're there for medical reasons — they can be flexible with check-in and check-out timing when hospital schedules are involved.
